issue.title: OIDC adapter stabilization

labels.name: kind/epic
labels.description: Large issue with links to sub-issues

issue.body:
### Description
Users are actively experimenting with the OIDC adapter and have reported a number of bugs.

### Analysis
A complete [list of the OIDC issues](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea/oidc).

### Tasks
- [x] OIDC `web-app` applications do not work with IdentityServer 4 (#6087, depends on #6526)
- [x] OIDC `web-app` applications do not work with Okta (#5277, depends on #6526)
- [x] OIDC `web-app` applications do not work with Microsoft ADFS (#6603, depends on #6526)
- [x] `quarkus-keycloak-authorization` does not work with reactive routes (#5809)
- [x]  `integration-tests/oidc-code-flow` test is unstable (#5926)
- [x] OIDC `web-app` applications have to support a static `redirect-url` (#5733)
- [x] OIDC `web-app` applications do not work with Auth0 (#5829)
- [x] `quarkus-keycloak-authorization` does not work with Keycloak 8 (#5868)
- [x] HTTP 403 should be reported if token has no expected custom role claim (#5750)
- [x] `quarkus-keycloak-authorization` claim information point read body NPE (#5959)

body: Regarding the original problem (NPE when obtaining the body) the cause of the exception is that the body needs to be read first by a handler (blocking). The solution I found is to reuse the `VertxInputStream` from Resteasy extension.

I think I have a prototype that might work. But not sure whether or not it is the best way to achieve it. Here are the changes https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/compare/master...pedroigor:issue-5959?expand=1.

Basically, after reading the request from the security layer, we set a buffered stream in the routing context so that later it can be reused. There is a change to Resteasy that checks whether or not the buffered stream is set and if so, uses it instead of trying to read again from the connection.

issue.title: Use Vert.x BodyHandler
issue.body:
Fixes #5959

This change allows the body handler to be used for Undertow
and RESTEasy standalone. When the request is fully buffered
it can be consumed multiple times, which allows keycloak
to also process it.
